title: Constitutions & rights
examples: What is the difference between a written and unwritten constitution?
Can a constitution guarantee my right to free speech?
How do people challenge unfair laws?

explain.say: A constitution is a set of fundamental rules for a country.

draw.text: Constitution: Basic rules for a country.

explain.say: Some constitutions are written down in a single document.
Other constitutions are unwritten, made up of many laws and customs.
A key job of a constitution is protecting basic human rights.
If rights are threatened, citizens can appeal to courts for help.

items: Decision upholds or changes the law

explain.say: In everyday life, traffic laws are like mini-constitutions.

draw.text: Real life: Traffic laws guide safety.

faq.q: What is the main difference between written and unwritten constitutions?
faq.a: A written constitution is all in one book, while an unwritten one comes from many sources like laws and traditions.
asks: Where do unwritten rules come from?

faq.q: Can a constitution give me rights that are not in the document?
faq.a: No, the constitution is the main source defining those guaranteed rights for all citizens.
asks: Does the constitution make up rights?

faq.q: If a law breaks my rights, what should I do?
faq.a: You can usually challenge that law through the court system to have it reviewed for fairness.
asks: Who can stop an unfair law?
How do I fight a bad law?

faq.q: Are constitutions the same everywhere in the world?
faq.a: No, every country develops its own unique set of rules and governing principles.

faq.q: What does 'fundamental' mean in this context?
faq.a: It means the rights are so important they cannot easily be taken away by the government.

facts: Constitutions establish the basic framework for a government.
Written constitutions are compiled in a single, formal document.
Unwritten constitutions draw rules from common law and customs.
Constitutions often contain sections dedicated to fundamental human rights.

quiz.say: A set of basic rules for a country is called a:
quiz.why: The constitution is the overarching set of rules for a nation.

wrong.0: A custom is an unwritten practice, not the whole legal framework.
wrong.2: A statute is just one type of law, not the whole system.
wrong.3: A decree is usually an order from a single leader, not the whole system.

quiz.say: If a country's rules are mostly based on long-held traditions and laws, it has a:
quiz.why: Unwritten constitutions gather rules from many sources, including tradition.

wrong.1: This implies all rules are in one book, which is not always true.
wrong.2: A Bill of Rights is only one part, focusing only on rights.
wrong.3: A treaty is an agreement between countries, not a country's internal law.

quiz.say: A citizen whose rights are violated by a new law should first seek help from:
quiz.why: Courts are the established body designed to review and protect citizen rights.

wrong.1: The Prime Minister makes laws, but the courts judge if they are fair.
wrong.2: Police enforce laws, but courts interpret if the law is constitutional.
wrong.3: The media can raise awareness, but courts provide legal protection.
